title: The DP02 contact-and-consent row, the consent vocabulary, the members of the letter append and the unserved status are in no source
source: Ownership Map v1 (P1 rwb-source-data: tables contact_point_ext, interaction; operations GET /data-products/{productCode}/records, POST and GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions); TSD P1 v3 T-A.2 API-P1-010 and T3.5; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-019, DF-INT-012, DF-INT-017, DF-INT-028, DF-INT-029, LOV-CONDUCT, LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, LOV-SEND-STATUS); legacy story RWB-E2-021 sections 4, 7, 11 and 12
section: s3 Preconditions; s7 AC1 to AC7; s8 BR7, BR9; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy loop read the postal contact point and its consent in process and wrote one ledger entry that it then updated from Sent to Delivered or Unserved. The target splits that into a DP02 read and an append-only ledger, and no source fixes four things the split needs. First, API-P1-010 answers a DataProductRecordPage for a case and names no row type for a contact point, so the members contactKey, contactType, consentStatus, verifiedAt, extensionPresent and consentAt, the vocabulary GIVEN, WITHDRAWN and UNKNOWN, and the rule that resolves it from consent_given and consent_at are unstated; the legacy story carries only the boolean DF-EXT-015 and the word WITHDRAWN of AC5. Second, interaction has no notice_type and no hold_reason column, so the notice type DEMAND and the hold reason CONTACT_STOP_X1 that the legacy entry named have no home and are carried as summary text. Third, the members the append requires are unstated: whether conductCheck is mandatory on a LETTER entry, whether a BLOCKED entry carries a deliveryStatus or an externalRef at all, and what a barcode longer than the varchar(60) of DF-INT-029 does. Fourth, LOV-SEND-STATUS holds SENT, DELIVERED, READ and FAILED only, while the legacy story records Unserved with the delivery statuses UNDELIVERABLE and PENDING, so the target value for an unserved letter and the place of the ACE proof result code are unsettled. The DP02 stamp of the answer (dataAsOf, productStatus from data_product_load) is fixed by FSD P1 A2.2 and A2.14 and is not part of this row.
evidence: TSD P1 v3 T-A.2 API-P1-010: 'Read the rows of one data product for a case, read through the v_ace_* views and the extension tables, masked by role (E1-037), with the product's freshness stamp', query caseId, page, size, response DataProductRecordPage; TSD P1 T3.5 gives contact_point_ext with consent_given boolean and consent_at; LDM v8 rows DF-INT-011 summary varchar(2000), DF-INT-012 conduct_check LOV-CONDUCT, DF-INT-028 delivery_status varchar(15) with LOV-SEND-STATUS, DF-INT-029 external_ref varchar(60); LOV-SEND-STATUS values SENT, DELIVERED, READ, FAILED; LOV-CONDUCT values PASSED, BLOCKED, NOT_APPLICABLE; legacy RWB-E2-021 AC4 'the ledger entry has conduct check BLOCKED', AC5 'consent status WITHDRAWN', AC3 'Unserved with delivery status UNDELIVERABLE', AC6 'Unserved with delivery status PENDING', section 11 writes interaction.channel, summary and conduct_check only.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-021 (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, section 11, section 12)
proposed: Publish the DP02 contact-and-consent row and its vocabulary in RWB-P1-E1016-CON, add the required-members table of the LETTER append to RWB-P1-E1066-CON, and either add an UNSERVED value to LOV-SEND-STATUS with its version or confirm the FAILED mapping with the ACE result code in source_ref; until then the shapes and the mapping of sections 12.1 and 13 hold and the point closes against the reference-data contract of DP-07.

title: The interaction ledger is published on two different operation paths
source: Ownership Map v1 (P1 rwb-source-data: POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions, GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions); RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P1-E1066-CON section 12.1 (POST /interactions, GET /interactions/{entryId}); RWB-P6-E2021-CON section 12.2 and section 12.8 (the ledger write it fakes); RWB-P3-E2021-APP fragment (ops_consumed POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions)
section: s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.8 Contract fakes; s19 Out of scope
description: The Ownership Map lists the ledger append of P1 as POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions and its read as GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions. The writer story of the same service publishes POST /interactions and GET /interactions/{entryId}, and the loop of RWB-P6-E2021-CON fakes the write against that resource; the case story of RWB-P3-E2021-APP declares the same consumed row. Two clients therefore build against two paths for one resource, and a third read (the case ledger in case_seq order) exists in neither story. The owning service is P1 in every source, so the conflict is one of naming and not of ownership. This story publishes the Ownership Map paths, and its append and case read carry the two rows the loop needs.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 P1 rows: 'GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions' and 'POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions'; RWB-P1-E1066-APP section 12.1 rows POST /interactions and GET /interactions/{entryId}; RWB-P6-E2021-CON section 12.2 'POST the interaction ledger write, P1 rwb-source-data, faked (DP-18)' and section 12.8 'rwb-source-data WireMock'; legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12 calls InteractionLedgerApi.record(UUID, InteractionRecord) in process.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-021 (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, section 12)
proposed: Settle one path family for the ledger in RWB-P1-E1066-CON, realign the fake of RWB-P6-E2021-CON and the consumed row of RWB-P3-E2021-APP to it, and keep the case-scoped form so that the case check and the scope are part of the address; until then the Ownership Map rows are the published ones and the append and the case read of section 12.1 hold.
